officers.name: Daniel Bustos
bio: Daniel is a third-year Electrical Engineering student at UCCS, U.S. Army veteran, and President of the Wire Lion Engineering Club. His interests include power systems, electronics, embedded systems, and hands-on engineering projects that turn concepts learned in the classroom into practical experience.

As president, Daniel is passionate about creating opportunities for students to build projects, develop technical skills, network with professional engineers, and gain experience outside of the classroom. His goal with Wire Lion is to create an environment where students at any experience level can get involved, learn from one another, make mistakes, and develop the confidence to tackle increasingly challenging projects.
For Daniel, engineering is not just about earning a degree; it's about building something, figuring out why it did not work the first time, and working together until it does.

officers.name: William McGinley
bio: Billy is a senior Electrical Engineering student at UCCS with a passion for understanding how things work and turning ideas into real, working projects. His interests range from power systems to electronics, with a particular appreciation for hands-on projects that involve designing, building, testing, and troubleshooting from the ground up.

As an officer of the Wire Lion Engineering Club, Billy enjoys working alongside other students, sharing knowledge, and taking on projects that challenge the team to learn new skills. For him, engineering is about curiosity, creativity, collaboration, and, most importantly, having fun while building something cool.

advisors.name: Leslie Tekamp
bio: Leslie (Les) Tekamp is a Teaching Professor in the UCCS Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering and serves as the faculty advisor for the Wire Lion Engineering Club.
He teaches courses including ECE 2021 Computer-Based Modeling in C, ECE 3610 Engineering Probability and Statistics, and CS 2060 Programming with C.
